title: Average of pointwise minima at most minimum of averages
statement:
Let $N \ge 1$ and $T \ge 1$ be integers, and let $f(t,j)$ be a real number for each $t \in \{1,\dots,T\}$ and each $j \in \{1,\dots,N\}$. Then averaging over $t$ before minimising over $j$ can only increase the value:
\[
  \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^{T} \min_{1 \le j \le N} f(t,j)
  \;\le\;
  \min_{1 \le j \le N} \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^{T} f(t,j).
\]
hypotheses_covered: N ≥ 1 (index set j nonempty, from NeZero N)
f a real-valued function of t and j
replaced:
For any $f : \mathrm{Fin}\,T \to \mathrm{Fin}\,N \to \mathbb{R}$ and $T > 0$,
\[
  \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \min_{j} f(t, j)
  \;\le\;
  \min_{j} \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} f(t, j).
\]
